name: Point of sale
summary: One bonded order at the counter: buyer and seller, no processor in between.
description: The simplest trade Figaro secures: a buyer and a seller resolve a purchase directly. Both lock a bond worth more than the trade, so honoring it is the only profitable move — no card network, no payment processor, no chargeback department. At checkout the buyer picks one of the four ways the modalities clause offers for the goods to change hands: consumed on-site, picked up, delivered or virtual. The composition carries no courier order, so a delivery is the seller's own. One signature resolves it.

faq.question: How does a walk-in pay at the counter?
faq.answer: With a wallet app on their phone. They open your page, pick the item, and commit; you hand it over; they resolve on the spot. Their phone is the card reader, and nobody sits between you.

faq.question: What does the buyer need?
faq.answer: A wallet, a little ETH for gas, and twice the item's price in the token you price in. That is the buyer's bond, and the price is paid to you out of it when they resolve. A buyer without a wallet cannot use this assembly.

faq.question: What do I put up, and when am I paid?
faq.answer: A bond of twice the price, refunded whole when the buyer resolves, in the same transaction that pays you. The buyer's bond, less the price it carried, is refunded at the same moment.

faq.question: What if the buyer walks off without resolving?
faq.answer: Nothing moves. Their bond, twice the price, stays locked with yours, where resolving would have cost them the price alone. They keep the item; you are out the item, and your bond stays locked too. Hand over after they commit, and resolve before they leave; the assembly is built for the two steps to happen at the counter.
